analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation only: date bumps in docs/architecture/inference.md and docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md, a new table row in inference.md (about line 1387), and a new paragraph in prefix-cache.md (head lines 670-690). Nothing executable or configurable changed in the supplied units.

The prefix-cache paragraph describes a described scheduler behavior: `demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens` makes a dense Qwen request end a range at the deepest aligned boundary at least 64 tokens below its prompt end. This yields more or deeper complete-checkpoint donations to the paged encrypted store. Relevant threat is T-041 (TB-007, A-001).

Security reading of the described behavior:
- Checkpoints are written only if the store would write them, so existing storage floors, per-donation gating, HMAC-keyed names, cacheSalt scoping and the 30-minute TTL are stated as unchanged.
- The change may shift which prefix lengths are cached, so it could slightly alter the same-account TTFT oracle granularity (SEC-035, already accepted). It does not add a new disclosure class on its face.
- No at-rest metadata is described as changed.

The remaining inference.md text in the replayed units (MiMo tool schemas, Flint constraints, GLM tool validation, decode accounting) appears to be descriptive documentation of pre-existing or separately reviewed code. I saw no claim in it that weakens an authorization, attestation or encryption control. It explicitly says restoring original schemas grants no tool, media or memory-admission bypass.

The code paths cited (DemandedShortCheckpointRange.swift, EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift) were not supplied. An integration or code pass should confirm that the demanded boundary cannot bypass the store floor, the adoption/benefit gating, the salt scoping, or the disk and endurance guards. T-041's detection_hint covers SSD donation policy.

No findings.
